concept.title: Writing on the Page
concept.shortdesc: Type, make lists and steps, apply styles, and insert any element your document type allows — from the keyboard, the toolbar or the right-click menu.

strow.stentry: Enter in a paragraph or list item
A new paragraph or item (without the original's @id)
Enter in an empty last list item
Leaves the list: a paragraph after it
Enter at the end of a title
Starts the short description (or the next paragraph)
Backspace at the start of a block
Joins it to the previous one
Tab / Shift+Tab in a list item
Nests the item in the previous one / moves it out (in a table: next / previous cell)
Undo / redo on the page (and in the document)

section.title: Styles and the Insert Menu
section.p: The Style list turns the current paragraph into what the DTD allows there — a note, a code block, a lines block… Insert adds any block element the DTD allows after the current block: the common ones first, then all of them grouped by domain.

section.title: The Right-Click Menu
section.p: Right-click on the page, or press the Menu key or Shift+F10. The cursor moves where you clicked, unless you clicked inside the selection, which the menu then acts on.

fig.title: Wrapping selected words in a phrase element

image.alt: The right-click menu on two selected words, with the Wrap in submenu open: common phrase elements first (xref, ph, keyword, term, uicontrol…), then submenus by domain.

dlentry.dd: Elements copied in the editor keep their structure and attributes; HTML pasted from other applications becomes paragraphs, lists, code blocks and bold/italic/code.
Every block element the DTD allows after the current block.
Every phrase element the DTD allows at the cursor (xref, ph, uicontrol, filepath, term…): around the selected text or, with nothing selected, with its name as placeholder text to type over.

dlentry.dt: Select, Move up, Move down, Remove tags (keep content), Delete
dlentry.dd: On the element at the cursor, whose name is shown above them.
The for that element; the text editor at that place.

section.p: The menus follow the document type exactly — a <title> offers phrases but no <xref>, a <note> takes paragraphs and lists but no <section> — and an item that would break the structure is greyed out. In every menu, the arrow keys move, → opens a submenu, ← or Escape closes it, Enter runs the item, and typing the start of a name jumps to it.
